outcomes: One field declaration drives runtime validation, TypeScript inference, and generated documentation
A browser bundle uses the same declaration without pulling server-only code into the graph
Validation failures name the field that failed instead of reporting that the whole payload is wrong
The fast path used for per-request validation accepts and rejects exactly what the reference validator does
nonGoals: Being a general-purpose schema language for data outside a Putnami workload
Emitting JSON Schema, OpenAPI, or client code from this package
Promising that a pre-1.0 minor release keeps the previous schema vocabulary

requirements.text: A field declared with Default() is optional in input and always present in output; a field with neither Default() nor Optional() is required and its absence is an error.
A value whose type does not match its declaration is reported as a field-level error and the value is kept as authored rather than silently replaced.
String inputs are coerced to the declared type only when the caller enables coercion; an uncoercible value is still reported as a type mismatch.
Validation recurses into nested objects, arrays, and maps, reporting the failing path and rejecting a collection whose container type is wrong.
Repeated validation of the same schema produces the same verdict, and a constraint never mutates a value the caller supplied.
A compiled validator agrees with the interpreted validator on accepted values, rejected values, applied defaults, and coercion, and delegates any case it cannot reproduce exactly.
The browser entry point exports the shared vocabulary and no server-only utility, and the shared modules import no Node built-in.
The JSONL build-hook protocol is reachable only from the dedicated hooks subpath and is not exported by the root or browser barrels.
